deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

description.description: A description of the auth config.
description.rationale: Free-form descriptive text for the auth config. Descriptive metadata with no security impact.

display_name.description: The name of the auth config.
display_name.rationale: Human-readable name for the auth config, used for identification only. No security impact.

expiry_notification_duration.description:
User can define the time to receive notification after which the auth config becomes invalid. Support up to 30 days. Support granularity in hours.

A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits, ending with 's'. Example: "3.5s".
expiry_notification_duration.rationale: Defines how long before auth-config expiry the user is notified. This is a notification-timing preference and does not enforce credential validity or rotation, so it is not a security policy target.

location.description: Location in which client needs to be provisioned.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

override_valid_time.description:
User provided expiry time to override. For the example of Salesforce, username/password credentials can be valid for 6 months depending on the instance settings.

A timestamp in RFC3339 UTC "Zulu" format, with nanosecond resolution and up to nine fractional digits. Examples: "2014-10-02T15:01:23Z" and "2014-10-02T15:01:23.045123456Z".
override_valid_time.rationale: A team-provided timestamp overriding the credential's expiry. It is a per-credential operational value, not a generic security toggle, and cannot be meaningfully constrained by a platform policy.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Identifier of the GCP project the resource belongs to. It is a reference; we do not constrain which project a team deploys into via a generic policy.

visibility.description: The visibility of the auth config. Possible values: ["PRIVATE", "CLIENT_VISIBLE"]
visibility.rationale: Setting visibility to 'PRIVATE' minimizes unauthorized access and exposure.

client_certificate.encrypted_private_key.description: The ssl certificate encoded in PEM format. This string must include the begin header and end footer lines.
client_certificate.encrypted_private_key.rationale: The PEM-encoded private key (encrypted) for the client certificate. This is a secret value supplied by the team, not a configurable security toggle; a platform policy cannot meaningfully constrain its contents, and pinning a value would be overreaching.

client_certificate.passphrase.description:
'passphrase' should be left unset if private key is not encrypted.
Note that 'passphrase' is not the password for web server, but an extra layer of security to protected private key.
client_certificate.passphrase.rationale: The passphrase protecting the client certificate's private key. It is a secret value supplied by the team; a platform policy cannot meaningfully constrain a secret's contents, so it is not a policy target.

client_certificate.ssl_certificate.description: The ssl certificate encoded in PEM format. This string must include the begin header and end footer lines.
client_certificate.ssl_certificate.rationale: The PEM-encoded client SSL certificate. It is a team-supplied certificate payload, not a configurable security toggle; a platform policy cannot meaningfully constrain its contents.

decrypted_credential.credential_type.description: Credential type associated with auth configs.
decrypted_credential.credential_type.rationale: Only approved credential types are allowed to ensure strong, secure, and supported authentication methods

decrypted_credential.auth_token.token.description: The token for the auth type.
decrypted_credential.auth_token.token.rationale: The token value for token-based auth. It is a secret payload supplied by the team; a generic policy cannot constrain a secret's contents and the resource will not authenticate with a blank token anyway, so it is not a meaningful policy target.

decrypted_credential.auth_token.type.rationale: Using secure authentication token types ensures proper authorization standards are enforced.

decrypted_credential.jwt.jwt_header.description: Identifies which algorithm is used to generate the signature.
decrypted_credential.jwt.jwt_header.rationale: The JWT header is a free-form, team-supplied JSON fragment describing the token's signing algorithm and type for the target system. A generic policy cannot meaningfully constrain its arbitrary contents, and the existing claim that HS256 should be mandated is incorrect (HS256 is a symmetric algorithm, not a secure default to pin).

decrypted_credential.jwt.jwt_payload.description: Contains a set of claims. The JWT specification defines seven Registered Claim Names which are the standard fields commonly included in tokens. Custom claims are usually also included, depending on the purpose of the token.
decrypted_credential.jwt.jwt_payload.rationale: A free-form set of JWT claims supplied by the team. A generic policy cannot meaningfully constrain an arbitrary claims document, so it is out of scope.

decrypted_credential.jwt.secret.description: User's pre-shared secret to sign the token.
decrypted_credential.jwt.secret.rationale: The pre-shared secret used to sign the JWT. It is a secret payload supplied by the team; its contents cannot be constrained by a generic policy, so it is not a policy target.

decrypted_credential.oauth2_authorizatio.description: The auth url endpoint to send the auth code request to.
decrypted_credential.oauth2_authorizatio.rationale: The OAuth2 authorization URL the auth-code flow sends requests to. This is an endpoint reference specific to the team's identity provider; we do not constrain references to external endpoints and a generic policy cannot know the correct URL.

decrypted_credential.oauth2_authorizatio.description: A space-delimited list of requested scope permissions.
The token url endpoint to send the token request to.

decrypted_credential.oauth2_client_crede.description: Represent how to pass parameters to fetch access token Possible values: ["REQUEST_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED", "REQUEST_BODY", "QUERY_PARAMETERS", "ENCODED_HEADER"]
decrypted_credential.oauth2_client_crede.rationale: Only secure request types should be used to transmit credentials. Types like 'ENCODED_HEADER' or 'REQUEST_BODY' ensures safer handling of credentials.

decrypted_credential.oauth2_client_crede.description: A space-delimited list of requested scope permissions.
The token endpoint is used by the client to obtain an access token by presenting its authorization grant or refresh token.
Token parameters for the auth request.
A list of parameter map entries.

decrypted_credential.oidc_token.audience.description: Audience to be used when generating OIDC token. The audience claim identifies the recipients that the JWT is intended for.

decrypted_credential.oidc_token.service_.description: The service account email to be used as the identity for the token.

decrypted_credential.service_account_cre.description: A space-delimited list of requested scope permissions.
Name of the service account that has the permission to make the request.

decrypted_credential.username_and_passwo.rationale: The password value for username/password credentials. It is a secret payload supplied by the team; its contents cannot be constrained by a generic policy, so it is not a policy target.
The username for username/password credentials. It is a team-supplied identifier value, not a configurable security control, so it is not a policy target.
